sentences.text: Avalonnectes was a small rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur that possessed only 18 to 19 dorsal vertebrae, a low number unique among its relatives.
This animal is considered one of the oldest known plesiosaurs because its fossils represent the earliest occurrence of the group.
The holotype specimen NHMUK 14550 includes the back of a skull and a nearly complete, articulated postcranial skeleton preserved in three dimensions.

Fossils were collected at Street in Somerset from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation. The genus Avalonnectes was named by Benson, Evans, and Druckenmiller in 2012, with Avalonnectes arturi as the type species. The name Avalonnectes combines 'Avalon', an island from King Arthur legends near the discovery site, with the Greek word for 'swimmer'. The species name 'arturi' honors paleontologist Arthur Cruickshank, who began restudying British Lower Jurassic plesiosaurs in the 1990s.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Avalonnectes is a basal member of the rhomaleosaurid family.

Avalonnectes lived approximately 199.6 to 198 million years ago during the earliest Hettangian stage, just after the Triassic-Jurassic boundary. The fossil record for Avalonnectes spans from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago during the Hettangian stage.
